See also: lycee and Lycée

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
lycée
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From French lycée. Doublet of lyceum.

Noun

[edit]

lycée (plural lycées)

  1. A public secondary school in France.

Translations

[edit]
a public secondary school in France

  • Esperanto: liceo (eo)
  • French: lycée (fr) m
  • German: Lyzeum (de) n
  • Greek: λύκειο (el) n (lýkeio)
  • Indonesian: sekolah menengah (id)
  • Japanese: 高等学校 (ja) (こうとうがっこう, kōtōgakkō), 中学校 (ja) (ちゅうがっこう, chūgakkō)

  • Portuguese: liceu m
  • Russian: лице́й (ru) m (licéj)
  • Spanish: liceo (es) m

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
lycée
Wikipedia fr

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin lyceum, from Ancient Greek Λύκειον (Lúkeion) (the name of a gymnasium, or athletic training facility, near Athens where Aristotle established his school), from Λύκειος ("Lycian" or "wolf-killer").

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /li.se/
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Homophone: lycées
  • Hyphenation: ly‧cée

Noun

[edit]

lycée m (plural lycées)

  1. a public secondary school

Derived terms

[edit]
  • lycéen

Related terms

[edit]
  • collège

  • → Arabic: لِيسيه (līsēh)
  • → Ottoman Turkish: لیسه (lise)
    • Turkish: lise
      • → Northern Kurdish: lîse
  • → Persian: لیسه (lise)
  • → Romanian: liceu
